messages.message: ### Step 2: Direct Translation Translate each source line into Bulgarian, guided by the Reference Translation and Step 1 analysis. Output: ONE Bulgarian line per source line (preserve line count and end punctuation). Rules: - Follow the meaning from Reference Translation. - For "so X that Y": keep resultative structure, do NOT convert to "because". - No internal punctuation; copy only end punctuation from source.
и тогава ще видиш онези които са доволни в огъня защото се надяват да дойдат всеки път когато е към благословения народ.

### Step 3: Word Table & Coverage Check Build a word table from Step 2 translation, mapping each source word to its target equivalent. Output: ONE Markdown table (all lines combined). Columns: [Source Word] | [Contextual Definition] | [Target Word/Phrase] | [Back-Translation] | [Status: OK/MISSING/WRONG/GRAMMAR/UNNECESSARY] Mark GRAMMAR for agreement errors (gender, number, case) or other grammatical mistakes. Mark UNNECESSARY for elements present in source but not needed in target language (e.g., articles that target language omits naturally). After the table, list any MISSING, WRONG, GRAMMAR, or UNNECESSARY items.

| Source Word | Contextual Definition (from Step 1) | Target Word / Phrase (Bulgarian) | Back‑Translation (Eng.) | Status | |-------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|--------------------------|--------| | e | coordinating conjunction “and then” | **и тогава** | “and then” | OK | | vederai | future 2nd sg. of *vedere* “you will see” | **ще видиш** | “you will see” | OK | | color | demonstrative pronoun “those (people)” | **онези** | “those” | OK | | che (rel.) | relative pronoun “who/that” | **които** | “who” | OK | | son | present copula “are” | **са** | “are” | OK | | contenti | adjective “contented, satisfied” | **доволни** | “content” | OK | | nel | preposition “in” + article “the” | **в** | “in” | OK | | foco | noun “fire” | **огъня** | “the fire” | OK | | perché | causal conjunction “because” | **защото** | “because” | OK | | speran | 3rd pl. present of *sperare* “they hope” | **се надяват** | “they hope” | OK | | di | infinitive marker “to” | **да** | “to” (infinitive marker) | OK | | venire | infinitive “to come” | **дойдат** | “to come” | OK | | quando | temporal adverb/conjunction “whenever” | **всеки път когато** | “every time when” | OK | | che (idiom) | particle in *quando che* (no lexical meaning) | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | sia | subjunctive of *essere* “may be” | **е** | “is” (potential) | OK | | a | preposition “to” | **към** | “to/towards” | OK | | le | definite article, fem. plural “the” | — | — | **UNNECESSARY** | | beate | adjective “blessed” (definite) | **благословения** | “blessed” (missing definite article) | **GRAMMAR** | | genti | noun “folk, people” (definite) | **народ** | “people” | OK |

### Items Requiring Attention - **UNNECESSARY**: - *che* (idiomatic particle in “quando che”) – no Bulgarian counterpart needed. - *le* – Bulgarian does not use a separate definite article before a plural noun.
- **GRAMMAR**: - *beate* rendered as **благословения** lacks the required definite article suffix **‑т** for “the blessed folk” (should be **благословеният**).
All other source words are correctly represented in the Bulgarian translation.
